explain.say: Some atoms are unstable, like a wobbly tower of blocks. To settle down, their centres, called nuclei, throw out radiation. There are three main kinds, and they are very different at getting through things. Let us fire each one at some barriers.

explain.say: Look at the sheet of paper. Alpha particles are big and slow: two protons and two neutrons stuck together. They crash into atoms so often that a sheet of paper, or a few centimetres of air, stops them. What stops alpha?

explain.say: Paper, yes! Next, the aluminium. Beta particles are fast electrons shot out of the nucleus. They zip through paper but a few millimetres of aluminium stops them. Which barrier stops beta?

explain.say: Aluminium, great! Now the thick lead. Gamma rays are waves of energy, like super-powerful light, with no mass and no charge. They pass through paper and aluminium. Thick lead or concrete cuts them down a lot, but never quite to zero. Which is the hardest to stop?

explain.say: Gamma, exactly! But alpha does the most damage close up, because it knocks electrons off atoms so easily. Wow fact: many smoke alarms hold a tiny alpha source; smoke blocks the alpha, and the alarm sounds. Challenge: which radiation would you use to check paper thickness in a factory?

faq.q: What are alpha, beta and gamma?
faq.a: Alpha is two protons and two neutrons, beta is a fast electron from the nucleus, and gamma is a high-energy electromagnetic wave.

faq.q: Why is alpha stopped by paper?
faq.a: Alpha particles are big, slow and strongly charged, so they hit atoms constantly and lose their energy very quickly.
A few millimetres of aluminium stops beta particles.

faq.q: Why is gamma so hard to stop?
faq.a: Gamma rays have no mass and no charge, so they rarely interact with atoms. Only thick lead or concrete reduces them much.

faq.q: Which radiation is used in smoke alarms?
faq.a: Many smoke alarms use a small alpha source, americium-241. Smoke absorbs the alpha particles, the current drops and the alarm sounds.
asks: How does a smoke alarm use radiation?

facts: Alpha is stopped by paper, beta by a few mm of aluminium, and gamma is reduced by thick lead or concrete.
Alpha radiation is the most ionising; gamma is the most penetrating.
